notes: §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR12: "Following the unsuccessful execution of a READ statement, the content of the associated record area is undefined, the key of reference is undefined for indexed files, and the file position indicator is set to indicate that no valid next record has been established." Only the third clause is observable, through the next format 1 READ (§1985:IX.4.5.4 GR4 a: "If the file position indicator indicates that no valid next record has been established, execution of the READ statement is unsuccessful", status 46). Every failing exit of IndexedConnector.ReadSequential and ReadRandom (47, 46, 10, 23, 30) returns through FileConnector.Unsuccessful, which calls KeyedConnector.InvalidateFilePosition before it assigns the status; that clears the indicator's validity and arms FileConnector.SequentialReadGuard, so the next sequential READ answers 46 until an OPEN, a START or a successful READ repositions. KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRead stores the record area in the success branch only, so the area keeps its content, which undefined permits. The one case 2023 excepts (a record operation conflict leaves the indicator unchanged) cannot occur at 85: FileRegistry.RecordLocksSetUnder sets locks only under a LOCK MODE clause, and that clause, SHARING and the READ lock phrases are refused at 85 (COBOL0900), so the rule holds without exception as 1985 prints it. Probed at --std 85: a READ NEXT after the at end condition, after a random READ's invalid key (23) and after a 46 each answer 46; a successful random READ after a failure restores sequential reading. The witness fails a random READ with 23 in dynamic access and gets 46 on the READ NEXT that follows.

next.reason: CHANGED under the round-1 ruling, difference 2: this rule is the 1985 statement of the indicator's value after an unsuccessful READ, which round 1 quoted as the 1985 side of that difference. 1985, with no exception: 'Following the unsuccessful execution of a READ statement, the content of the associated record area is undefined, the key of reference is undefined for indexed files, and the file position indicator is set to indicate that no valid next record has been established' (§1985:IX.4.5.4 GR12). 2023: 'Unless otherwise specified, at the completion of any unsuccessful execution of a READ statement, the content of the associated record area is undefined, the key of reference is undefined for indexed files, and the file position indicator is set to indicate that no valid record position has been established' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR18), and it is otherwise specified for the record operation conflict, where 'The READ statement is unsuccessful' and 'The file position indicator is unchanged' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR10). The words that differ are 'Unless otherwise specified' and 'unchanged' against 'set to indicate that no valid next record has been established': a case removed from the 1985 result, and its result changed. This rule's own text adds a second result to its sequential and relative siblings, and the same case changes it too: 1985 'the key of reference is undefined for indexed files', 2023 for the conflict 'The key of reference for indexed files is unchanged' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR10), an undefined result made a defined one; outside the conflict GR18 keeps the 1985 words. A program with no post-1985 syntax reaches the condition: with no SHARING phrase or clause 'the implementor shall define the sharing mode that is established for each file connector' (§2023:14.9.27.4 GR23); with no LOCK MODE clause 'the type of record locking for that opening of a shared file associated with that file connector is defined by the implementor' (§2023:12.4.5.9.4 GR1); and when 'the record identified for access is locked by another file connector', 'the record operation conflict condition exists' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR9). The earlier KEPT rested on the conflict being 'record locking 1985 has no model of', the premise round 1 refuted with those three rules. Carried, and no ground: the record area is undefined in both, in the conflict case too ('The content of the associated record area is undefined', §2023:14.9.30.4 GR10); 'no valid record position' for 'no valid next record' is a term for the same thing in a standard that also reads PREVIOUS. The at end case is the other thing 'otherwise specified' and is no ground: 2023 leaves 'The file position indicator is set to indicate that no next or previous logical record exists' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR24) where this rule leaves 'no valid next record', and both editions state the same result for the READ that follows, status 46: 1985 'The preceding READ statement caused an at end condition' (§1985:IX.1.3.4), 2023 'if the previous READ or START statement for the file connector was unsuccessful, then the READ statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status is set to '46'' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR21; §2023:9.1.13.7 'The preceding READ statement referencing that file connector was unsuccessful'). GR24 is listed because it states the at end part of this rule's subject ('When the at end condition exists, execution of the READ statement is unsuccessful', with its NOTE 'The content of the associated record area is undefined as indicated in General rule 18'). Caveat, stated so that it is not mistaken for a missed observation: that same sentence of GR21 also gives 46 to the sequential READ that follows a conflict, so the ground is the indicator's stated result, exactly as in round 1's GR11 records, and not a different status on the next READ. Kind and 'to' are those of the sequential and relative GR12; only the key of reference ground is this record's own.
